_readme: This file is the site's content. Edit the text values (never the keys) to update copy without touching code. Anything wrapped in [Amber: ...] is a placeholder that needs real content before launch — search this file for '[Amber:' to find every one.

hero.headline: TELL CONGRESS: SUPPORT THE KARLY RAIN WOOD ACT
hero.ask: Ask your members of Congress to support and help advance the Karly Rain Wood Act, S. 5245.
reasons: [Amber: one punchy sentence — reason #1 the bill matters]
[Amber: one punchy sentence — reason #2 the bill matters]
[Amber: one punchy sentence — reason #3 the bill matters]

lookupStep.title: Find your lawmakers
lookupStep.helpText: We'll look up your 2 U.S. Senators and 1 U.S. Representative — we never store your address.
lookupStep.inputPlaceholder: e.g. 12345 or 123 Main St, Springfield, IL
lookupStep.errorNoMatch: We couldn't match that to a congressional district. Double-check your ZIP or try your full street address.
lookupStep.errorGeneric: Something went wrong on our end looking that up.
lookupStep.manualFallbackLabel: Look up your representatives directly on Congress.gov

messageStep.title: Personalize and send your message
messageStep.subjectLine: Please Support the Karly Rain Wood Act – S. 5245
messageStep.letterBody:
I'm writing as your constituent to ask you to support and help advance the Karly Rain Wood Act, S. 5245.

[Amber: insert 2-3 sentence plain-language summary of what the bill does and why it matters]

This bill matters to our community, and I'm asking you to co-sponsor it and push for a vote. Please let me know where you stand.

Thank you for your time and your service.
messageStep.personalizeBoxSubtitle: Optional but encouraged: tell them why this matters to you, your family, or your community.
messageStep.personalizeNote: Congressional offices count individual, personalized messages very differently from identical form letters — a sentence or two in your own words makes this count more.

promptChips.starter: As a parent, this issue is personal to me because

promptChips.label: Karly's story moved me
promptChips.starter: Karly's story moved me, and I'm asking you to act because

messageStep.sendHelpText: Most congressional offices require their own secure contact form. We'll copy your finished message and open each office's official page so you can paste it in — usually just a few taps.

items.question: What is the Karly Rain Wood Act?
Why does my message need to be personalized?
items.answer: Congressional staff read every message that comes in, but they weigh personal, original messages more heavily than identical form letters when gauging genuine constituent concern. A sentence or two in your own words goes a long way.

items.question: Is my information stored or sold?
items.answer: [Amber: confirm and insert real privacy answer — this site does not store your address; confirm what, if anything, is retained from the message form.]

items.question: I don't live in a state with a sponsor — should I still take action?
items.answer: Yes. Every constituent message to every office, sponsor or not, helps build momentum and signals nationwide support.
